title: one file per task, and no hand-kept copy of the task list
acceptance: Every pull request conflicts with every other one because each edits the same two shared regions: the tail of design/tasks.json's single task array, and the task table in design/design.md, which is a hand-kept copy of it. With main requiring up-to-date branches, each merge turns every open pull request into a conflict. On 2026-09-24 this forced repeated hand resolution and force pushes, and once silently dropped a design section. The captain approved the first-principles fix: parallel work must never write the same text. Its own spec is design/tasks/T-090.json, added in this pull request.

design/tasks.json is replaced by design/tasks/<id>.json, one file per task, holding exactly today's entry for that task (same keys, same values). Adding a task adds a file; revising a task edits only its file. The migration is mechanical and lossless: a test checks that the concatenation of the new files, ordered as today, equals the old array.

The task table in design/design.md is removed and replaced by a sentence pointing to design/tasks/ and to a command that prints the table on demand (bin/fm.sh tasks, grouped by milestone, with id, title and dependencies). Nothing generated is committed, so nothing can conflict. bin/ci.sh's agreement check becomes: every task file parses, its id matches its file name, its dependencies exist and there are no cycles.

Every reader switches to the directory through one shared helper in bin/fm-config.sh (list tasks, get one task), and board/server.ts reads it the same way. Gate 4 reads the task's scope from design/tasks/<id>.json on the branch under test, keeping today's rule, now from the task's own file. The readers found by a search on 2026-09-24 are all in this task's scope; search again, and stop and name any reader outside the scope.

Pull requests already open when this lands carry edits to design/tasks.json. The design.md paragraph that replaces the table says how such a branch is brought over: its own entry moves to its own file. This task's own branch is the first to do it.

Evidence is this pull request's required GitHub check and the seven gates. Tests written to fail first: the lossless migration; the id and file-name agreement; a missing dependency and a cycle turn ci red; two branches that each add a task merge with no conflict (a real git fixture); gate 4 reads scope from the task's own file; bin/fm.sh tasks prints the table. The worker does not run the suite itself.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.
